# D3 revision (2026-08-16) — the fused default retires; bm25 is the shipped default

**Decision.** `locate`'s default retriever changes from `fused` to `bm25`.
`--retriever=exact|fused` remain available as measurement arms (S8); the
fused arm is retained for comparability and marked retired-as-default.

**Basis, and nothing else.** Pre-registered study c36
(doi:10.5281/zenodo.21969901; the bake-off deposit's results document): on the registered 141-document
public corpus with a fresh 115-question blind set, the fused arm trailed its
own BM25 leg by 7.8 pp localization (85.2% vs 93.0%, McNemar p = 0.0225),
failing the frozen prediction "fusion never costs localization." The
pre-registered ablation registry rule — *RRF fusion: retire if fused ≤ best
single* — fires; this document is the design act the rule requires.

**Scope of the retirement.** This configuration (RRF k=60 fusing a ranked
BM25 leg with a heuristically-scored exact leg) on this corpus class. The
RRF constant was never swept (conceded in the study); a rank-aware exact
signal or swept-k fusion is successor territory and re-enters the default
path only through a fresh registration. Per the program's rule: **the
framework never grades itself** — no future default change without a
registered result behind it.

**Changes.** `src/core/query.js` default + contract text;
`bin/mentu-nav.js` help; tests pin the default arm (`strategy === "bm25"`)
and two test defects surfaced by the flip were corrected (a fixture that
mutated the corpus between paired measurements, and a fused-arm ordering
assertion). 44/44 green.
